question.problem: A particle $P$ of mass $0.25\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a resultant force. The displacement of the particle is given by $({t}^{4}-2{t}^{2}+2)\,m,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the work done by the force between the times $t=1\,s$ and $t=2\,s.$
question.worked_solution:
The work-energy principle states that the work done by a resultant force on a particle equals the change in the particle's kinetic energy. That is,

$$
W=Δ\,\text{KE}
$$

where the change in kinetic energy of a particle is given by

$$
Δ\,\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2}
$$

and $m$ is the particle's mass, ${v}_{0}$ is its initial velocity, and ${v}_{1}$ is its final velocity.

The displacement of the particle is given by $x(t)={t}^{4}-2{t}^{2}+2,$ where $t$ is time in seconds.
We find the velocity $v(t)$ of the particle by differentiating the displacement with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-2{t}^{2}+2) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-4t\end{aligned}
$$

So, the particle's initial velocity, at $t=1$, is

$$
{v}_{0}=v(1)=4(1)^{3}-4(1)=0\,m/s,
$$

and final velocity, at $t=2$, is

$$
{v}_{1}=v(2)=4(2)^{3}-4(2)=24\,m/s.
$$

Therefore, by the work-energy principle, the work done by the force between these times is

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =Δ\,\text{KE} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0.25\cdot (24)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0.25\cdot {0}^{2} \\  & =72-0 \\  & =72\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
